4	# IPhO 2026, Problem 3 (Pm-T paramagnetic torus), Subquestion C.1
5	
6	Carnot refrigeration cycle $1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 4 \to 1$ of the paramagnetic
7	torus (Pm-T) in the $H$-versus-$T$ plane (Figure 3b).  The task of C.1
8	(0.2 pts) is to mark $T_h$ and $T_c$ on the $T$ axis of the $H$-vs.-$T$
9	diagram and to identify the processes on which $Q_h$ (magnitude of the
10	heat delivered to the hot reservoir) and $Q_c$ (magnitude of the heat
11	absorbed from the cold reservoir) are transferred.
12	
13	Official answer (T3 solution + marking scheme C.1: "correctly label
14	temperatures on graph" 0.1, "specify heat flow portions in diagram" 0.1):
15	
16	* $T_c = T_2 = T_3$ and $T_h = T_4 = T_1$ — "the respective temperatures
17	  of the isothermal processes $2 \to 3$ and $4 \to 1$" (official solution
18	  text);
19	* $Q_c = |Q_{2\to3}| = Q_{2\to3}$ — heat is *absorbed* from the cold
20	  reservoir on the isothermal leg $2 \to 3$;
21	* $Q_h = |Q_{4\to1}| = -Q_{4\to1}$ — heat is *delivered* to the hot
22	  reservoir on the isothermal leg $4 \to 1$.
23	
24	## Figure 3b geometry (official source page `T3_page-3.png`)
25	
26	$H$ is plotted vertically against $T$ horizontally.  Vertices $2$ and $3$
27	share the left $T$-coordinate (leg $2\to3$ is vertical, hence isothermal);
28	vertices $1$ and $4$ share the right $T$-coordinate (leg $4\to1$ is
29	vertical, hence isothermal).  Legs $1\to2$ and $3\to4$ are the two curved
30	adiabats of the Carnot cycle.  The field magnitude decreases along
31	$1\to2$ and along $2\to3$ and increases along $3\to4$ and along $4\to1$;
32	on the $T$ axis the pair $\{2,3\}$ sits to the left of the pair $\{1,4\}$.
33	
34	## Physical model extracted from the chapter
35	
36	* Named quantities (dimensional roles; measured magnitudes are real
37	  scalars):
38	  - `Th`, `Tc`: hot- and cold-reservoir temperatures (kelvin), $T_c<T_h$.
39	  - `Qh`, `Qc`: *magnitudes* of the heat delivered to the hot reservoir
40	    and absorbed from the cold reservoir (joule).
41	  - `Q12`, `Q23`, `Q34`, `Q41`: *signed* heats transferred into the torus
42	    along the four legs (joule; into-the-torus positive).
43	  - `T v`, `Hmag v`, `Mmag v`: scalar readouts of temperature, applied
44	    field magnitude and magnetization magnitude at vertex $v$.
45	  - `n`: amount of paramagnetic ions (mol); `K`: material constant of the
46	    equation of state; `V`: fixed torus volume (m³); `μ₀`: vacuum
47	    permeability.
48	* Governing laws (assumptions, never the C.1 answer):
49	  - Equation of state of the ideal paramagnet: $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$
50	    (given in the problem context; part of the setup and of the later
51	    C.2 proof route, not needed for the C.1 signs themselves).
52	  - Isothermal heat relation of part B.1 (previous-part result): at fixed
53	    temperature $T$, when the field changes from $H_i$ to $H_f$ the heat
54	    transferred *into* the torus is
55	    $Q = -(\mu_0 n K/(2T))(H_f^2 - H_i^2)$ — its *sign* content is what
56	    selects the heat-flow directions below.
57	  - Adiabatic legs transfer no heat (definition of adiabatic).
58	  - Reversible two-reservoir Carnot structure: each isothermal leg
59	    exchanges heat with one of the two reservoirs at the reservoir's own
60	    temperature, with the refrigeration orientation (absorb $+Q_c$ from
61	    the cold reservoir, deliver $Q_h$ to the hot reservoir) — stated as a
62	    per-leg disjunction that does *not* decide which leg is cold.
63	* Current target conclusions (conclusion side only):
64	  $T_1 = T_4 = T_h$, $T_2 = T_3 = T_c$; $Q_c$ is absorbed on $2\to3$
65	  ($Q_{2\to3} = +Q_c > 0$) and $Q_h$ is delivered on $4\to1$
66	  ($Q_{4\to1} = -Q_h < 0$); no heat is transferred on the adiabatic legs.
67	
68	## Derivation route recorded for the proof phase
69	
70	By the B.1 law on leg $2\to3$ with $H_3 < H_2$ (figure) the heat into the
71	torus is strictly positive (heat absorbed); by the reservoir-exchange
72	disjunction the leg can then only be the cold one:
73	$T_2 = T_3 = T_c$, $Q_{2\to3} = +Q_c$.  Symmetrically, on $4\to1$ the
74	field increases ($H_4 < H_1$), the B.1 heat is strictly negative (heat
75	delivered), so the leg is the hot one: $T_4 = T_1 = T_h$,
76	$Q_{4\to1} = -Q_h$.  An independent cross-check comes from the $T$-axis
77	readout $T_2 < T_1$ together with $T_c < T_h$.
78	
79	## Sibling-file conflict (redraft flag for plan/review)
80	
81	The existing file `problem_IPhO_2026_3_C_2.lean` (and its blueprint
82	chapter) formalizes Figure 3b with the *opposite* process-kind assignment:
83	`Figure3bAssignment` declares legs $1\to2$, $3\to4$ isothermal and
84	$2\to3$, $4\to1$ adiabatic, while its own C.1 prerequisite quote records
85	the official answer used here.  The official solution ("the isothermal
86	processes $2\to3$ and $4\to1$", with $T_c=T_2=T_3$, $T_h=T_4=T_1$) and
87	the Figure-3b page image (vertical legs $2\to3$, $4\to1$) agree with the
88	present file, so `3_C_2`'s figure assignment (and its per-leg heat /
89	adiabatic-law fields, which attach to the swapped legs) should be
90	redrafted against this C.1 contract.  Files do not import each other
91	(previous parts are natural-language prerequisites only), so there is no
92	compile-time dependency.
93	-/

117	  T : Vertex → ℝ

136	structure TorusParams where
137	  /-- Vacuum permeability $\mu_0$. -/
138	  μ₀ : ℝ
139	  /-- Amount of paramagnetic ions, $n$ (mol). -/
140	  n : ℝ
141	  /-- Material constant $K$ of the equation of state $TMV = nKH$. -/
142	  K : ℝ
143	  /-- Fixed volume $V$ of the torus (m³). -/

145	  μ₀_pos : 0 < μ₀
146	  n_pos : 0 < n

150	/-- The equation of state of the ideal paramagnet, $T\,M\,V = n\,K\,H$.
151	A *governing law* assumed about the model, not a local definition: it
152	relates the three vertex readouts at every state of the cycle. -/
153	def EquationOfStateParamagnet (p : TorusParams) (T H M : ℝ) : Prop :=
154	  T * M * p.V = p.n * p.K * H
155	
156	/-- Isothermal heat relation from part B.1 (governing law / previous-part
157	result, assumed — not proved — here): when $H$ changes from $H_i$ to $H_f$
158	at constant temperature $T$, the heat transferred *into* the torus is
159	
160	$Q = -\frac{\mu_0\,n\,K}{2T}\,(H_f^2 - H_i^2)$.
161	
162	The heat argument is signed (into the torus positive), so the direction of
163	the transfer (in vs. out) is carried by the sign: heat is absorbed when
164	the field decreases and released when it increases.  This sign content is
165	the physical input that identifies the heat-flow directions of C.1. -/
166	def IsothermalHeatIntoTorus (p : TorusParams) (T Hi Hf Q : ℝ) : Prop :=
167	  Q = -(p.μ₀ * p.n * p.K / (2 * T)) * (Hf ^ 2 - Hi ^ 2)
168	
169	/-- Reversible two-reservoir heat exchange on an isothermal leg of the
170	Carnot refrigeration cycle (governing law of the model): a leg at
171	temperature `Tleg` along which the heat `Qleg` flows into the torus
172	exchanges heat with one of the two reservoirs *at the reservoir's own
173	temperature* (reversibility of the Carnot cycle), and the refrigeration
174	orientation fixes the sign — the torus *absorbs* $+Q_c$ from the cold
175	reservoir on a leg at $T_c$, or *delivers* $Q_h$ to the hot reservoir on a
176	leg at $T_h$ (heat into the torus $-Q_h$).
177	
178	The disjunction is the law; it is stated for *any* isothermal leg and does
179	not assert which leg of Figure 3b sits at which reservoir temperature —
180	that identification is the content of subquestion C.1. -/
181	def ReservoirExchange (Tc Th Qc Qh Tleg Qleg : ℝ) : Prop :=
182	  (Tleg = Tc ∧ Qleg = Qc) ∨ (Tleg = Th ∧ Qleg = -Qh)
183	
184	/-- The model hypotheses for subquestion C.1: reservoir data, the heats
185	along the four legs, the Figure-3b readouts, and the physical laws the
